newsitem.title: CANADA: MMT ban bill near top of Canadian govt agenda.
newsitem.headline: MMT ban bill near top of Canadian govt agenda.

text.p: The Canadian government put a controversial bill to ban the the import and interprovincial trade of the gasoline additive MMT near the top of its agenda on Monday.
It put the bill on a list of three pieces of legislation for debate today in the House of Commons, Parliament's lower chamber.

A parliamentary clerk said the House would not necessarily get around to debating it today. But the fact that the government included it among three of the 13 bills it has pending signalled the importance attached to it.
MMT, methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl, is made by the U.S. firm Ethyl Corp and imported and distributed by its subsidiary Ethyl Canada.
Ethyl says MMT helps the environment, but the auto industry says it gums up auto emission diagnostic equipment. The government has come down on the side of the carmakers.
The bill now is at "third reading" -- the final stage for the bill before passage by the House, though opposition parties can delay it through procedural moves as they did in late 1995.
